Computational Verification#

IQCs with terminal cost can be used to prove stability, performance, and invariance properties of dynamical systems. These stability proofs are based on finding solutions to Linear Matrix Inequalites.

Boundedness/Stability with IQCs#

Let \(G_R\) = \((A_R, B_R, C_R, D_R)\) be a linear system, let \(\rho> 0\) be a convergence rate, and \(\mathcal{O}\) be an operator. The exponentially weighted iterates \((\ov p, \ov q)\) related by \(\ov p_k \in \rho^{-k} \mathcal{O}(\rho^{-k} q_k)\) for the operator \(\mathcal{O}\). This pair \((\ov p, \ov q)\) satisfies the IQC \((\Psi(\blam), M(\blam), X(\blam))\) for any \(\blam \in \Lambda(\rho)\).

The \(\rho\)-weighted interconnection of \((G_R, \mathcal{O})\) is

\[\begin{split}\begin{align} \mat{c}{\ov{x}_{k+1} \hl \ov p_k} &= \mat{c|c}{\rhoi A_R & \rhoi B_R \hl C_R & D_R}{\ov{x}_k \\ \ov q_k}, & \ov q_k & \in \rho^{-k} \mathcal{O}(\rho^{k} \ov p_k). \end{align}\end{split}\]

The system \(G_\Psi := \Psi(\blam) \mat{c}{G_R \\ I}\) has input \(q\), output \(r\), and states \((\psi, \ov{x})\). The state-space representation of \(G_\Psi\) is

\[\begin{split}\begin{align} G_\Psi: & & \mat{c}{\psi_{k+1} \\ \ov{x}_{k+1} \hl r_k} &= \mat{c|c}{A(\blam) & B(\blam) \hl C(\blam)& D(\blam)} \mat{c}{\psi_k \\ \ov{x}_k \hl q_k} \\ & & \mat{c|c}{A & B \hl C& D} & := \mat{cc|c}{ A_\psi & B_\psi^p C_R & B^p_\psi D_R + B^q_\psi \\ 0 & \rhoi A_R & \rhoi B_R \hl C_\psi(\blam) & D^p_\psi(\blam) C_R & D^\psi_p(\blam) D_R + D^\psi_q(\blam)} \end{align}\end{split}\]

If there exists a quadratic function \(V(\psi, \ov{x})\) and a tolerances \(\epsilon \geq 0, \epsilon_q > 0\) such that for all trajectories \((\psi_k, \ov{x}_k)_{k \in \N}\) of \((G_\Psi, \mathcal{O})\) with \(\psi_0=0\) we have

\[\begin{split}\begin{align} V(\psi_{k+1}, \ov{x}_{k+1}) - V(\psi_k, \ov{x}_k) &\leq -r_k^\top M r_k - \epsilon \norm{q_k}^2_2, \\ V(\psi_k, \ov{x}_k) - \psi_k^\top X \psi_k & \geq 0, \end{align}\end{split}\]

then we observe for all time horizons \(T \in \N\) that

\[\begin{split}\sum_{k=0}^{T-1} V(\psi_{k+1}, \ov{x}_{k+1}) - V(\psi_{k}, \ov{x}_k) &\leq - \sum_{k=0}^{T-1} r_k^\top M r_k - \epsilon \norm{q_k}_2^2, \\ V(\psi_{T}, \ov{x}_T) - V(\psi_0, \ov{x}_0) &\leq -\sum_{k=0}^{T-1} r_k^\top M r_k - \epsilon \norm{q_k}_2^2\end{split}\]

Adding the valid IQC relation for \(\mathcal{O}\) to the above inequality yields

\[\begin{split}\textstyle \sum_{k=0}^{T-1} V(\psi_{k+1}, \ov{x}_{k+1}) - V(\psi_{k}, \ov{x}_k) &\leq - \sum_{k=0}^{T-1} r_k^\top M r_k - \epsilon \norm{q_k}_2^2, \\ V(\psi_{T}, \ov{x}_T) - V(\psi_0, \ov{x}_0) &\leq - \epsilon \textstyle\sum_{k=0}^{T-1} \norm{q_k}_2^2 + \psi_{T}^\top X \psi_T.\end{split}\]

This relation ensures boundedness of \((\psi, \ov{x})\):

\[0 \leq V(\psi_{T}, \ov{x}_T) - \psi_{T}^\top X \psi_T \leq V(\psi_0, \ov{x}_0)- \epsilon \textstyle \sum_{k=0}^{T-1} \norm{q_k}_2^2\]

If there exists \(\epsilon_M, \epsilon_X > 0\) such that

\[\begin{split}\begin{align} V(\psi_{k+1}, \ov{x}_{k+1}) - V(\psi_k, \ov{x}_k) &\leq -r_k^\top M r_k - \epsilon \norm{q_k}^2_2 - \epsilon_M (\norm{\psi_k}_2^2 + \norm{\ov{x}_k}_2^2), \\ V(\psi_k, \ov{x}_k) - \psi_k^\top X \psi_k &\geq \epsilon_X (\norm{\psi_k}_2^2 + \norm{\ov{x}_k}^2_2), \end{align}\end{split}\]

then summing from \(0\) to \(T-1\) yields the relations

\[\begin{split}\epsilon_X (\norm{\psi_k}_2^2 + \norm{\ov{x}_k}^2_2) &\leq V(\psi_{T}, \ov{x}_T) - \psi_{T}^\top X \psi_T, \\ V(\psi_{T}, \ov{x}_T) - \psi_{T}^\top X \psi_T & \leq V(\psi_0, \ov{x}_0)- \textstyle \sum_{k=0}^{T-1} \left(\epsilon \norm{q_k}_2^2 + \epsilon_M \norm{\psi_k}_2^2 + \epsilon_M \norm{\ov{x}_k}_2^2\right),\end{split}\]

This then proves asymptotic convergence \(\lim_{k\rightarrow \infty} (\psi_k, \ov{x}_k) = 0\).

IQC Analysis (General)#

The quadratic function \(V\) is expanded into

\[\begin{split}V(\ov{x}, \psi) = \mat{c}{\psi \\ \ov{x}}^\top \mat{cc}{P_{\psi \psi} & P_{\psi \ov{x}} \\ P_{\psi \ov{x}}^\top & P_{xx}} \mat{c}{\psi \\ \ov{x}}.\end{split}\]

The IQC Analysis to verify asymptotic convergence of the exponentially weighted interconnection is to find a matrix \(P\) and coefficients \(\blam \in \Lambda(\rho)\) such that

\[\begin{split}\begin{align} \mat{cc}{I & 0 \\ A(\blam) & B(\blam) \\ C(\blam) & D(\blam)}^\top \mat{ccc}{-P & 0 & 0\\ 0 & P & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & M(\blam)} \mat{cc}{I & 0 \\ A(\blam) & B(\blam) \\ C(\blam) & D(\blam)} \prec 0 \end{align}\end{split}\]
\[\begin{split}\begin{align} \mat{cc}{P_{\psi \psi} - X(\blam) & P_{\psi \ov{x}} \\ P_{\psi \ov{x}}^\top & P_{xx}} & \succ 0 \end{align}\end{split}\]

Bisection can be used to find a minimal \(\rho\) certifying asymptotic convergence.

The analysis program is convex in \(\blam\) for fixed \(\rho\) if

  • \(\Lambda(\rho)\) is convex for each \(\rho\),

  • either \(\Psi(\blam)\) is \(\blam\)-independent, or \(M(\blam)\) is \(\blam\)-independent.

Parameterizing \(A_\Psi(\blam), B^p_\psi(\blam), B^q_\psi(\blam),\) will cause a bilinearity between the variables \(\blam\) and \(P\).

Outlook for Optimization#

The operator class \(\F\) satisfies a family of IQCs \((\Psi(\blam), M(\blam), X(\blam))\) with respect to signal transformation matrix \(\ell\). These \((\Psi(\blam), M(\blam), X(\blam), \ell)\) terms are assembled from the individual operators \(\{F_i\}_{i=1}^s\). The worst-case linear convergence rate for any algorithm \((F, G)\) with \(F \in \F\) can be upper-bounded by solving an IQC analysis problem on the following plant \(G_\Psi\) with input \(\ov q\) and output \(r\):

\[\begin{split}\begin{align} \mat{c}{\ov{x}_{k+1} \hl \ov z_k} &= \mat{c|c}{\rhoi \Acl & \rhoi \Bcl \hl \Ccl & \Dcl}\mat{c}{\ov{x}_k \\ \ov w_k},\\ \mat{c}{\ov p_k \\ \ov z_k} &= \mat{cc}{\ell_{pq} & \ell_{pw} \\ \ell_{zq} & \ell_{qw}} \mat{c}{\ov q_k \\ \ov w_k}, \\ \mat{c}{\psi_{k+1} \hl r_k} &= \mat{c|cc}{A_\psi& B_\psi^p & B_\psi^q \hl C_\psi & D_\psi^p & D_\psi^q} \mat{c}{\psi_k \hl \ov p_k \\ \ov q_k}. \end{align}\end{split}\]

Conservatism can be reduced by increasing the filter order \(\Psi\) when considering valid relations.
